## 🌎 Geopolitics

### Saudi Arabia halts crude oil exports amid global energy shock

Saudi Arabia has stopped all crude oil exports as of mid-September 2026, marking an unprecedented move in global energy markets. The halt threatens to tighten oil supplies worldwide and immediately impacts energy costs for major importers including India, which relies on Saudi Arabia for roughly 20% of its crude imports. Brent crude futures have spiked in response, signaling broader economic shocks across supply chains dependent on energy pricing.

**Why it matters.** India's current account and macro health depend on stable energy import costs; with the rupee-dollar dynamics tied to crude prices, any supply shock from Saudi Arabia cascades through consulting and fintech valuations tied to macro stability. For quant research, this creates immediate volatility in energy futures and currency pairs. The move also forces India to accelerate diversification away from Middle Eastern suppliers and deepens India's energy dependency on Russia—a geopolitical shift with long-term implications for Quad positioning and US-India trade talks.

**Action.** Watch Brent crude intraday volatility and crude import cost trends from CEIC Data or RBI bulletins. Check Indian Airlines and shipping stocks for exposure. Monitor whether India's government signals emergency talks with other OPEC producers or accelerates renewable energy capex targets—this could reshape energy-sector equity positioning for the next 24 months.

*Sources: [makesenseworld.substack.com](https://makesenseworld.substack.com/p/state-of-geopolitics-13-september) · [zerofox.com](https://www.zerofox.com/intelligence/monthly-geopolitical-report-september-2026/)*

### BRICS Summit 2026 tests India's strategic autonomy as Putin, Xi reshape Global South bloc

India is hosting the 18th BRICS Leaders Summit on September 12-13 with Russian President Putin confirmed and Chinese President Xi Jinping expected to attend. The summit, themed "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability," marks India's attempt to steer BRICS toward measurable outcomes beyond political theater while navigating deepening US-China tensions and managing its security ties to Russia amid sanctions pressure. India's 2026 chairship operates on a fragile balancing act: maintaining Quad alignment with the US while preserving strategic autonomy in BRICS.

**Why it matters.** For India-market exposure, BRICS bloc coordination directly affects rupee stability, capital controls risk, and sectoral opportunities in Global South infrastructure deals. India's consulting and fintech sectors are positioned as intermediaries in BRICS cross-border payments and trade settlement alternatives to Swift—a structural macro shift. Xi and Putin's presence signals alignment on de-dollarization, which tests India's ability to hedge between Western capital markets and BRICS settlement mechanisms, a core constraint for quant research modeling emerging-market volatility.

**Action.** Monitor outcomes from the summit on trade, digital currency frameworks, and development bank priorities. Track how India balances BRICS statements on commodity pricing with Quad security commitments. Watch for any announcements on BRICS currency baskets or alternative payment rails—these reshape forex hedging assumptions for India-exposed portfolios.

*Sources: [organiser.org](https://organiser.org/2026/09/08/379373/world/brics-summit-2026-india-leads-strategic-reforms-to-power-global-south-prosperity-amid-geopolitical-upheavals/) · [thequint.com](https://www.thequint.com/opinion/brics-2026-india-russia-china-us-geopolitics-multipolar-world) · [ey.com](https://www.ey.com/en_gl/insights/geostrategy/geostrategic-analysis)*

## 🧠 Artificial Intelligence

### Three AI Giants Announce Safety Coordination Framework to Pre-Release Test High-Capability Models

OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google DeepMind declared September 15 that they have been in formal coordination for weeks on AI safety standards, establishing private working groups since July to build infrastructure for independent pre-release testing and safety auditing. Chris Lehane, OpenAI's global policy chief, stated the three labs do not require antitrust waivers to coordinate on safety, citing "better to try to work together to prioritize safety." The coordination follows Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's published framework for slowing frontier AI development to avoid catastrophic risks, and reflects regulatory pressure under the proposed FRONTIER Act requiring independent verification organizations inside frontier labs.

**Why it matters.** This signals a structural shift in how frontier models enter production—from competitive opacity to coordinated pre-release gates. For system builders shipping agentic AI, this means frontier models will undergo external audit cycles before general release, creating harder dependencies on lab timelines. The framework legitimizes independent evaluators as formal requirements, not post-hoc additions. For enterprise teams, this reduces supply-chain volatility by binding capability release to verified safety checkpoints rather than business cycles alone. For lab researchers, this establishes peer review as a production dependency, shifting incentives from first-to-deploy to first-to-verify-safely.

**Action.** Monitor Anthropic's published safety evaluation criteria and protocols as they emerge—these become template for industry standards. Run your reasoning-critical systems (math, code, high-stakes decision-support) against Claude and GPT-6 Astra under their declared safety audit results, not just benchmark scores. Plan 2-4 week buffers into agentic AI deployments for pre-release testing; the coordination framework will push release timelines back and narrow the window for early adoption.

*Sources: [[https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/openai-says-it-s-working-with-anthropic-google-on-ai-safety](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/openai-says-it-s-working-with-anthropic-google-on-ai-safety)]([https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/openai-says-it-s-working-with-anthropic-google-on-ai-safety](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/openai-says-it-s-working-with-anthropic-google-on-ai-safety)) · [[https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/openai-anthropic-google-have-been-in-talks-on-ai-safety-for-weeks/](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/openai-anthropic-google-have-been-in-talks-on-ai-safety-for-weeks/)]([https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/openai-anthropic-google-have-been-in-talks-on-ai-safety-for-weeks/](https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/openai-anthropic-google-have-been-in-talks-on-ai-safety-for-weeks/)) · [[https://www.kuwaittimes.com/article/49820/business/openai-is-working-with-anthropic-google-on-ai-safety/](https://www.kuwaittimes.com/article/49820/business/openai-is-working-with-anthropic-google-on-ai-safety/)]([https://www.kuwaittimes.com/article/49820/business/openai-is-working-with-anthropic-google-on-ai-safety/](https://www.kuwaittimes.com/article/49820/business/openai-is-working-with-anthropic-google-on-ai-safety/))*

### AWS and NVIDIA Deploy 2 Million GPUs; AMD Signs Gigawatt-Scale Commitments to OpenAI and Anthropic

AWS and NVIDIA announced a major infrastructure expansion to deploy 2 million additional NVIDIA GPUs globally, deepening collaboration across AI factories, CPUs, networking, and robotics. Simultaneously, AMD secured multi-gigawatt commitments: OpenAI will deploy 1 gigawatt of AMD Instinct MI450 GPUs in H2 2026 under a multi-year agreement, with capacity scaling to 6 gigawatts total; Anthropic committed to purchasing up to 2 gigawatts of MI450 chips starting H1 2027, backed by up to $5 billion in investment. AMD's data center revenue doubled to $6.7 billion in the most recent quarter, cementing the vendor's foothold against NVIDIA's historical dominance.

**Why it matters.** This represents hard commitment to scaled agentic inference—2 million NVIDIA GPUs plus multi-gigawatt AMD deployments signal labs are pivoting from training to production serving. For architects building reasoning systems, this GPU doubling means sustained availability of compute through 2026-2027, reducing scarcity-driven design decisions. AMD's entry at scale breaks NVIDIA's monopoly on frontier lab capacity, enabling price competition and design flexibility around AMD's CDNA architecture—relevant if your inference loop tolerates ROCm or if you're optimizing for CapEx rather than locked-in CUDA. For infrastructure teams, this confirms the cost of agentic systems has shifted from training to inference at scale; plan cluster sizing for sustained multi-gigawatt deployments, not burst training.

**Action.** Benchmark your reasoning workloads on both NVIDIA H200 and AMD MI450 partitions if available through your cloud provider—cost-per-inference will diverge as AMD ramps production. Review OpenAI and Anthropic's deployment timelines (1-6 gigawatts through 2026-2027) to predict API capacity ceilings and price pressure. For on-premise deployments, lock AMD quotes now; CapEx arbitrage between NVIDIA and AMD will compress as both vendors scale.

## 🇮🇳 India

### Pixxel lands $100M Series C as Indian deeptech startups cross $412M in weekly funding

Bengaluru-based satellite imaging startup Pixxel closed a $100 million Series C from Temasek and Seraphim Space during the week of September 7-12, 2026. The round crowned a remarkable stretch: 24 Indian startups raised $412.81 million across that same five-day window, marking one of the strongest weekly periods for Indian startup funding in 2026. The surge spans space tech, fintech, AI enterprise software, climate tech, and deeptech, signaling capital has moved decisively toward harder technical problems.

**Why it matters.** For an AI engineer choosing between consulting gigs and joining an Indian startup, this moment resets expectations. Capital is no longer scarce for companies with defensible tech—it's competing to fund them. Pixxel's ticket size ($100M at Series C) and backer roster (growth-stage space funds) show the playbook: build proprietary earth observation AI, license to governments and enterprises, scale globally from India. Fintech, autonomous systems, and industrial AI are now swimming in the same capital pool. The constraint is no longer "will we raise" but "can we ship and retain engineers."

**Action.** Track Tracxn's weekly India funding reports for round size and sector trends. Review Pixxel's Series C announcement for valuation and breakdown of fund sources. Monitor which other spacetech or deeptech startups announce in September and October—they will benchmark round sizes and term sheets against Pixxel. Check whether Seraphim and Temasek follow Pixxel with follow-ons to other India deep-tech deals.

*Sources: [[Indian startups raised over $412 million from September 7 to September 12, 2026](https://indianstartupnews.com/funding/indian-startups-raised-over-412-million-from-september-7-to-september-12-2026-pixxel-tops-the-list-12528949)]([Indian startups raised over $412 million from September 7 to September 12, 2026](https://indianstartupnews.com/funding/indian-startups-raised-over-412-million-from-september-7-to-september-12-2026-pixxel-tops-the-list-12528949)) · [[Startups in India News]([Startups in India News) · [September, 2026](https://blog.mean.ceo/startups-india-news-september-2026/)](September, 2026](https://blog.mean.ceo/startups-india-news-september-2026/)) · [[Top AI News in India, September 2026](https://www.parikshitkhanna.com/post/top-ai-news-in-india-september-2026-10-developments-shaping-enterprise-ai-agentic-payments-data)]([Top AI News in India, September 2026](https://www.parikshitkhanna.com/post/top-ai-news-in-india-september-2026-10-developments-shaping-enterprise-ai-agentic-payments-data))*

### India Deep Tech Alliance pledges $1B to AI startups, 58% YoY funding surge validates ecosystem bet

The India Deep Tech Alliance has committed $1 billion USD in dedicated funding to Indian AI startups, to be deployed over three years. The commitment arrives as part of a broader $2.5B USD capital allocation to deeptech and arrives on the heels of a 58 percent year-over-year jump in AI funding throughout 2025. The move formalizes what had been grassroots momentum: deep tech now represents roughly 15 percent of India's overall VC-PE activity, a structural shift from fringe category to core allocation.

**Why it matters.** This is not a one-off fund or a startup announcement—it is institutional capital and policy alignment converging. For an AI engineer deciding whether to stay independent, join a B2B SaaS company, or co-found a deeptech play, the $1B IDTA commitment signals that the scaffolding exists. Government backing (through the IndiaAI Mission), institutional LPs (endowments, sovereign wealth, growth funds), and sector specificity (AI, manufacturing, climate, biotech) now all point the same direction. Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated 80 percent of India's startups are now AI-led, meaning competition for capital is fierce—but capital now exists.

**Action.** Pull the India Deep Tech Alliance inaugural report to see sector allocations and fund manager preferences. Monitor DPIIT and the IndiaAI Mission website for announcements on follow-on capital deployment and governance. Track which IDTA member funds (Lightspeed, Nexus, Accel, etc.) have revised their India AI allocation upward and review their recent portfolio announcements. Watch for Series A/B rounds announced in October-November from previous seed-stage AI startups, which will now have clearer funding paths.

## 📈 Markets

### US Treasury Breaks 2007 Barrier as Fed Rate Hike Looms

The US 10-year Treasury yield pierced 5.01% on September 15—the highest level since July 2007—sending shockwaves across global equities. The Dow Jones closed down 328 points (0.63%) to 52,093.11; the S&P 500 fell 0.45% to 7,585.73; and the Nasdaq dropped 0.78% to 25,981.57. India's Nifty 50 mirrored the weakness, closing down 279 points (-1.19%) at 23,118.60, while Sensex fell 777 points (-1.04%) to 74,003.82. The rupee weakened to 95.99 per dollar, and India's 10-year G-Sec yield climbed toward 7.1%.

**Why it matters.** The yield spike reflects a fundamental repricing of Fed rate expectations ahead of the FOMC decision announcement today at 2 PM ET. Futures are pricing two quarter-point hikes by year-end, starting with this week. For Indian macro—and the quant shops Shashank is tracking—this is an FII kill switch: higher US real rates make dollar-denominated debt cheaper relative to rupee assets, triggering capital flight precisely when domestic inflation (energy prices up 24% YoY) is forcing RBI to hold rates high. AI-infra names and domestic growth plays lose momentum when global funding costs rise; even the 0.24% Bank Nifty bounce signals defensive positioning. The 5% threshold is psychologically critical—last time 10Y was here, we were in peak post-crisis tightening.

**Action.** Fed's 2 PM announcement will clarify terminal rate guidance and the Summary of Economic Projections (dot plot). Watch Chair Warsh's press conference for language around disinflation path—if the Fed hints at a pause post-September, the curve could flatten and INR stabilize. Monitor the RBI's response: if India's yield premium over UST compresses below 200 basis points, expect accelerated FII selling in equities. Key level: if UST 10Y holds above 5.00%, expect another 50-100 bps of G-Sec outperformance.

### Saudi Pipeline Outages Lock In Sticky Inflation—Oil At 4-Month High

Brent crude climbed to $107.50 per barrel, its highest in four months, as the Saudi East-West pipeline remained offline following last week's attacks. The blockage has stripped 7 million barrels per day of Saudi export capacity from global markets. Compounding the supply crisis: the Iranian blockade on Persian Gulf tankers and the Red Sea corridor shutdown have forced OPEC producers, notably Saudi Aramco, to slash production to its lowest level since 1990. The US Energy Information Administration had forecast $90/bbl for H2 2026; current prices are running 20% above that forecast.

**Why it matters.** Energy prices are up 24% year-on-year (Federal Reserve's own data), and the collapse of the disinflation narrative is now the central bank constraint. For India, this is a double hit: crude import costs pinch the current account at exactly the moment INR weakness is accelerating, and it gives the RBI justification to hold rates higher for longer. Prop traders watching inflation-indexed instruments (ILS, TIPS) see the game theory clearly—central banks lose credibility if they cut while commodity tail-risks are live. India's fiscal room narrows if crude stays above $100. Longer oil duration means lower real yields globally, which perversely can support duration plays but starves equity multiples.

**Action.** Watch the Saudi Aramco and Saudi Aramco Energy Ventures for pipeline restart guidance—any announcement that the East-West line is operational intra-week could trigger a 3–5% crude selloff and a risk-on bounce in equities. The EIA's weekly crude inventory report (Wednesdays) will show whether refiners are forced to slow throughput; a counter-seasonal build would confirm supply anxiety. Track OPEC+ communications: if Saudi output remains capped, expect crude to hold the $105–$110 range through Q4 2026.

## 💹 Global Stocks

### SOFTBANK GROUP (TSE: 9984): -11.0% on OpenAI IPO delay to 2027

SoftBank Group plunged 11.0% on Monday-Tuesday (Sept 13-15), closing near ¥11,850, erasing last week's gains entirely. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated the company will not pursue a public listing in 2026, pushing a potential debut into 2027. SoftBank, which has committed nearly $65 billion to OpenAI through October, holds preferred shares worth that stake—shares that only convert to tradable common stock upon an IPO or related listing event. The delay leaves SoftBank's massive position locked in private equity limbo for at least another year.

**Why it matters.** This move exposes SoftBank's concentration risk in a single unlisted AI bet at precisely the moment when AI growth narratives are facing scrutiny around alignment and safety. The ripple cuts through Asia-ex-Japan sentiment: if Masayoshi Son's $65B wager on the *most valuable* AI company can be stranded as illiquid for another 12 months, the willingness of Asian capital to commit to long-dated tech ventures may cool. SoftBank's forced refinancing (repaying $25.9B bridge debt on Sept 15, replacing it with $11.87B over two years from 20 banks) signals lenders are now pricing longer-tail illiquidity into their terms. For Indian fintech and AI infrastructure investors watching Tier-1 Asia capital flows, this is a signal to tighten liquidity assumptions.

**Action.** Monitor SoftBank's next quarterly earnings (likely late October 2026) for management commentary on the OpenAI illiquidity impact and any revised valuation reserves. Check SoftBank's investor relations disclosures (Form 20-F filings with SEC, or Tokyo Stock Exchange announcements) for updates on the $40B bridge loan refinancing terms and any write-downs to the OpenAI investment. Watch for analyst downgrades on valuation multiples given the extended illiquidity. The critical level to watch is ¥10,900 support; a break below signals deeper loss-of-confidence selling.

### ASML HOLDING (NASDAQ: ASML, ENXTAM: ASML): +26.9% 30-day after second 2026 guidance raise

ASML shares reached $1,867.83 mid-September, up 26.86% over the past month, after the Dutch semiconductor equipment giant raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second time. The company now guides to €43.0–€45.0 billion in net sales with 54%–56% gross margin—up materially from prior guidance of €36.0–€40.0 billion and 51%–53% margin. Q2 2026 revenue of €9.3 billion (net income €2.9B) beat expectations, with orders described as "extremely strong" as customers accelerated capacity expansion for AI semiconductor manufacturing.

**Why it matters.** ASML's double guidance raise signals that the AI capex cycle is not only sustained but *accelerating*—contradicting recent market whispers of AI slowdown. Orders for both EUV (extreme ultraviolet) and DUV (deep ultraviolet) lithography remain robust enough for the company to target 30% capacity additions in both segments for 2026. This is the closest read on actual customer demand in the semis stack: ASML's customers are TSMC, Samsung, Intel, and Huawei. If they are pulling forward orders and raising capex amid AI safety warnings from OpenAI and Anthropic, it signals that enterprise and cloud AI spending—not hype—is driving equipment cycles. For Indian semiconductor and IT infrastructure players, this validates that the AI capex digestion story (Infra as the least crowded mega-cap beneficiary) still has legs.

**Action.** Check ASML's latest SEC filings (8-K from Sept 2026, 20-F annual) for updated customer concentration (% of revenue from TSMC, Samsung, etc.) and any commentary on China demand shifts. Track ASML's order backlog-to-revenue ratio in earnings releases; this metric best predicts near-term capex visibility. Critical technical level: $1,920 represents the 52-week high; failure to hold $1,750 would signal demand exhaustion. Monitor for analyst downgrades if gross-margin guidance proves too optimistic (EUV yields or pricing pressure could compress).

## 🏗 Tech & Startups

### Temporal Hits $12.55B Valuation as Agentic AI Workload Demands Explode

Temporal closed a $550 million Series E on September 14, 2026, at a $12.55 billion valuation in a round co-led by Lightspeed and Wellington Management with Goldman Sachs Growth Equity and Tiger Global. The workflow orchestration platform now serves 4,300 paying customers including OpenAI, NVIDIA, Netflix, and JPMorgan Chase, with annualized revenue exceeding $250 million and growing 200% year-over-year.

**Why it matters.** Temporal's explosion proves that infrastructure for running AI agents reliably is now table stakes. When OpenAI, NVIDIA, and JPM Chase all standardize on your orchestration layer, you're not a feature—you're the plumbing. The 200% YoY growth and $250M ARR at a $12.55B valuation shows investors will pay 50x ARR for de facto standards in AI infrastructure. For founders building agent platforms or AI applications, the playbook is clear: obsess over reliability and let the distribution come through customer adoption instead of sales noise.

**Action.** Monitor Temporal's next customer wins and market expansion moves. Their investor roster (a16z, Sequoia, Index, GIC, Sapphire Ventures) tells you who's betting on AI infrastructure consolidation. If you're building agents, examine whether you're routing execution through Temporal or rebuilding orchestration yourself—the cost of not standardizing may exceed the cost of adoption.

### Brain's Immune Cells Undergo Inflammatory Overhaul in Midlife, Reshaping Alzheimer's Risk

Researchers analyzing single-cell genomes from 30 human hippocampi found sweeping reorganization of the brain's genome architecture beginning at age 50, with the most dramatic shift occurring between ages 50 and 75. Embryonic-origin microglia—the brain's immune cells—declined substantially and were replaced by cells with pro-inflammatory molecular profiles. Simultaneous deterioration of the blood-brain barrier and 3D genome structure suggests a coordinated shift in immune function that correlates with when Alzheimer's disease risk sharply accelerates.

**Why it matters.** The study maps cellular and molecular changes that precede cognitive decline, shifting focus from late-stage Alzheimer's pathology to midlife immunological triggers. For longevity medicine, this signals the specific developmental window where preventive intervention might arrest neuroinflammation—critical information for trials of anti-inflammatory drugs, senolytic therapies, or immunomodulation protocols targeting ages 50-60. For AI builders in health, this provides mechanistic anchors for digital biomarker discovery: wearable-based tracking of inflammatory surrogates during this vulnerable decade.

**Action.** Read the peer-reviewed Science paper directly—it includes genome-wide datasets enabling secondary analysis. The UC San Diego and UC Irvine teams are publishing raw single-cell data, making this a high-value resource for computational genomics groups building predictive models of brain aging. This work justifies clinical trials of drugs that stabilize the blood-brain barrier or selectively deplete pro-inflammatory microglia in the 50-65 age range.

### Eleven Genetic Variants Controlling Gut Bacteria Linked to Cardiovascular Disease Risk

A genome-wide association study spanning 28,669 participants—12,652 from the Norwegian HUNT cohort and 16,017 from Swedish populations—identified eleven genetic variants that reproducibly regulate gut microbiota composition. Nine of these genomic regions are novel. Mendelian randomization analysis provided causal evidence that body mass index influences microbiota structure, and several variants showed association with cardiovascular disease, gluten intolerance, and hemorrhoid risk, establishing the gut microbiome-host genetics axis as actionable for cardiometabolic disease prevention.

**Why it matters.** This is the first large-scale, replicated identification of the genetic architecture controlling microbiota. For precision medicine, it means microbiome-based risk stratification for cardiovascular disease becomes genetically grounded rather than empirical. For AI-driven drug discovery, the specific genomic loci and their microbial phenotypes create clear targets for designer probiotics or genetic interventions. The causal link between BMI and microbiota composition also validates lifestyle interventions as mechanistically effective in the early cardiometabolic risk window.

**Action.** The HUNT study dataset and Nature Genetics paper provide the loci and effect sizes needed for biotech companies to design microbiota-targeted therapeutics and diagnostic panels. Clinicians should consider microbiome profiling in high-risk populations, now supported by host-genetic evidence rather than correlation. This justifies prospective trials of microbiota modification (probiotics, prebiotics, FMT) stratified by host genetics in pre-diabetic and cardiovascular risk cohorts.

### Astana AI Film Festival Becomes World's Largest AI Cinema Competition With 8,000+ Entries From 125 Countries

The Astana AI Film Festival (AAIFF 2026) announced 8,067 submissions from 125 countries ahead of its October 1-3 event, making it the world's largest competition dedicated to AI-generated cinema. Submissions came from 4,756 unique creators, with the United States leading at 1,395 entries, followed by Kazakhstan (829), India (702), China (550), and South Korea (349). The festival offers a combined $2.75 million prize and investment pool. Entries split into two categories: 3,138 under the theme "The Future Worth Living In" and 4,929 open competition films.

**Why it matters.** This is the first quantifiable signal of scale in the AI-generated video creator economy. 8K entries from this many countries in one year indicates rapid adoption of AI filmmaking tools across consumer and creator markets. The geographic distribution (U.S. dominance but significant growth in India, China, Korea) shows where AI content tools are penetrating fastest. For Shashank's audience: this reveals which platforms are likely to see distribution pressure (YouTube, TikTok, Vimeo will all compete for AI-native content), which tools are winning adoption, and where emerging creators are clustering. The prize pool itself signals investor conviction in AI cinema viability.

**Action.** Watch what wins and which AI tools are credited in the October awards. Track whether major platforms (YouTube, Amazon, Apple) court AAIFF winners for distribution. Monitor which geographic regions dominate the actual awards vs. submission counts—that's where creator bottlenecks exist. The open-competition vs. themed split is worth tracking too; themed work signals AI can execute on briefs, open work signals what creators want to make.
